subject: Uranus planet
title: Uranus Really Smells Like Rotten Eggs. That's the Least of Your Problems

scenes.text: One planet would smell like rotten eggs if you flew into it.
In 2018, astronomers using the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii studied light from Uranus's clouds.
They found hydrogen sulfide, the gas that makes rotten eggs stink.
But you'd never get a chance to smell it.
The air there is hydrogen, helium and methane, at about minus 200 degrees Celsius.
You'd suffocate and freeze first. The stink would be the last thing you noticed.

description:
Uranus's cloud tops contain hydrogen sulfide, the gas behind the smell of rotten eggs, detected in 2018 with the Gemini North telescope (Irwin et al., Nature Astronomy).
As the lead researcher said, suffocation and exposure in its roughly minus 200 C hydrogen, helium and methane atmosphere would get you first; Voyager 2 measured minus 224 C there, the coldest planetary atmosphere recorded.
Which planet should we smell next?
first_comment: Rotten eggs at minus 200 degrees. Which planet would you least like to visit?
